items.label: VHYL currency blocker confirmed -- deliberately NOT re-staged; VWRA re-confirmed USD and re-staged
items.detail: search_contracts for VHYL returns 3 separate exchange listings for the same Vanguard fund at 3 different prices -- LSEETF/GB $69.025, AEB/NL $80.45, EBS/CH (not priced) -- which is itself evidence the LSEETF/GB line (the one previously staged as instruction 101) is NOT trading in a consistent USD price alongside the other venues, consistent with the user's report that the LSE line settles in GBP. IBKR's own contract description for this share class reads 'VANG FTSE HDY USDD' (USD Distributing is the fund's underlying base currency), but that is the fund's accounting currency, not necessarily the LSE trading-line settlement currency -- the two can differ for Irish-domiciled UCITS funds with multiple listing venues, exactly the ambiguity the user flagged. VWRA, by contrast, carries the description 'VANG FTSE AW USDA' (USD Accumulating) and is Vanguard's specifically-USD-denominated share class of this fund (distinct from the GBP-denominated VWRL/VWRP tickers) -- reasonably confirmed USD. Deleted the stale VHYL draft (101) and did not replace it. Deleted and re-staged VWRA fresh at today's live price (955sh @ $192.00 limit GTC, instruction 100, ~$183,360) -- unchanged conviction, resized only for today's $191.66 last price (was $191.00/959sh on 09-16).
items.recommendation: Before ever resubmitting VHYL, verify its settlement currency directly in IBKR's own contract-detail screen (Contract Info > right-click > Description), since this session's tools cannot expose that field conclusively. See the USD-alternative research below for what to stage in VHYL's place once you confirm a fund choice.

items.label: USD-denominated income-fund alternatives to VHYL researched -- not staged, pending user fund choice
items.detail: Per the standing core-sleeve rotation thesis (VWRA = broad global accumulating core, second leg = income + diversification satellite), researched 3 real, live-quoted USD candidates to replace VHYL's role: (1) EIMI (iShares Core MSCI EM IMI UCITS ETF, LSEETF, USD Acc) -- $54.69, 1yr +36.51%, TER 0.18%, ~3,000 EM holdings, 0% distribution yield (accumulating, no income) -- Ireland-domiciled UCITS, same PFIC question mark as VWRA. (2) VYMI (Vanguard International High Dividend Yield ETF, NASDAQ) -- $103.13, 1yr +30.18%, TER ~0.22%, quarterly distributions at 3.61% yield, ~1,300+ developed+EM ex-US holdings -- US-domiciled 1940 Act fund, which very likely avoids PFIC treatment entirely since it is not a foreign fund (confirm specifics with a tax professional, but the domicile difference itself is real and material). (3) SCHY (Schwab International Dividend Equity ETF, ARCA) -- $32.51, 1yr +22.94%, TER 0.14% (cheapest of the three), quarterly distributions at 3.41% yield, ~100-holding developed-market-only dividend-quality screen (more concentrated, no EM) -- also US-domiciled.
items.recommendation: VYMI is the closer functional match to VHYL's original job (income + broad ex-US diversification including EM) and sidesteps the PFIC/UCITS question entirely by virtue of being US-domiciled -- lean toward VYMI as the lead candidate. SCHY is the lower-cost, more concentrated developed-only alternative if a tighter book is preferred. EIMI remains the accumulating/no-income option if the satellite's job shifts away from income generation. Domicile/tax treatment noted as an open question for the user to verify with a professional, not a settled conclusion. Not staged this run -- confirm a choice before the next run stages an order.
